note.saw: There was no earlier picture yet, only the brief: a group that is half compass geometry and half freehand flow, and a name that has to read instantly.
note.changing: The first full build: an eight-plus-eight point star wrapped in flowing rainbow rings and a flame aura, a rim of alien glyphs and tiny eyes, and a big scaled fish with lobed fins, a spiral-web eye and the name on two dark cartouches.
note.why: A coelacanth is all about its strange lobed fins and that extra little tail lobe, so a big side view shows them off best, and a temple of geometry suits a fish older than the dinosaurs.
note.idea: The coelacanth is a living fossil, so the first artist made it an ancient elder swimming across a jewelled star temple, its head and three-lobed tail breaking out over the halo, with SAVES and FISH carved into two dark bands above and below it.

note.saw: The name read instantly, but the fish was too slender with a thin rat-tail, the gill cover was a boxy blue frame like a TV screen, the lobed fins were round lollipops and the white spots almost vanished.
note.changing: A deeper, chunkier body; the gill cover redrawn as a curved rainbow edge around a big nautilus spiral; long leaf-shaped lobed fins with fringed rays; bold white blotches that each hold a tiny eye; and the name bands reshaped into pointed banners with spiral tips.
note.why: The real coelacanth is heavy and armored, with fins like little limbs and white blotches all over, so those features have to read at a glance before the psychedelic layers pile on.

note.saw: The fish finally looked like a coelacanth and SAVES / FISH read instantly, but the gill plate was an empty dark-blue patch, the white spots looked like tiny ghosts, the body felt flat and the eye was more of a target than a portal.
note.changing: The gill plate fills with rainbow contour stripes, a spinning chrysanthemum of petals rings the eye, the body gets an inner glow, the spots grow into bright blotches, rows of beads run along every aura band, and the letters gain a magenta 3D shadow.
note.why: DMT visions are described as glowing from inside and covered in living pattern, so every surface needs a second and third layer of detail, while the elder's eye should pull you in like a doorway.

note.saw: The magenta shadow made SAVES and FISH pop like a 1960s poster and the gill cover glowed, but the spots had sloppy shadows that didn't line up, the eye's petals looked like a cartoon sun, the aura was neat parallel stripes and nobody was watching yet.
note.changing: Four almond-eyed alien guardians now hold the tips of the name banners, wearing the star's points as pointed hats; curling rainbow tendrils break out of the aura; the eye's petals become finer and layered; and every scale gets a tiny pupil so the whole body looks back at you.
note.why: In DMT reports the visitor is always being watched by entities and the geometry seems alive, so the elder gets a court of guardians and its flame aura starts to curl and move.

note.saw: The guardians were too small to read as beings, more like teardrops with eyes, the tendrils mostly hid under the fins and banners, and the body was one even field of scales with nothing inside it.
note.changing: X-ray vision: the coelacanth's real backbone, a glowing tube it has instead of vertebrae, now shines through the scales with ghostly spines, chakra-like jewels of light and alien script along it. The guardians grow by a third with huge black eyes, and the aura band touching the fish turns into a gold-white glow with taller flames beyond.
note.why: Visionary art often shows the body's hidden light, and the coelacanth's backbone is one of the oldest on Earth, so lighting it up turns the fish into the ancient one from the inside out.

note.saw: The glowing spine with its seven jewels gave the body a backbone of light and the gold-white halo made the fish jump forward, but up close each guardian's two eyes crossed over each other into a muddle and drooped instead of slanting up.
note.changing: The guardians' faces are rebuilt with two separate black almond eyes slanting upward, brows, a third eye and a tiny mouth on violet skin. Spiral-web rosettes fill the banner tips, little eyes peek out between the rays of the tail and the spiny back fin, and each lobed fin carries its own white spot.
note.why: The beings have to read as faces in a split second or they are just decoration, and the real coelacanth is spotted right out to its fins, so the eyes and spots should keep going wherever you look.

note.saw: The guardians finally looked like little beings holding the banner ends, but zooming in four times on the corners showed flat background stripes, paisleys that were tiny black squiggles and tendrils like clumsy worms.
note.changing: Every background band gets a bright inner line and a row of beads in its gap, the paisleys grow and turn gold, magenta and cyan, the tendrils become tapered brush strokes curling into tight spirals, and seventy small four-point stars twinkle across the outer temple.
note.why: The brief asks for detail that still holds up at four times zoom, and hand-painted visionary art always has that outline-gap-outline rhythm, so even the quiet corners need their own little universe of pattern.

note.saw: The corners now held up close, but the inner glow had washed the body out to a pale lilac, so the white spots, the coelacanth's most famous marking, were losing their punch, and the fins lacked the bright edge glow the body had.
note.changing: The scales go back to a deep cobalt-to-ultraviolet with the glow toned down, the white blotches grow, and every fin gets a thin gold-white glow band just outside its dark outline.
note.why: A real coelacanth is deep steel blue with white blotches, so strong dark-against-light contrast is what makes it read as this exact fish, and a glowing edge on every fin lifts the whole silhouette off the rainbow aura.

note.saw: The fin glow made the silhouette crisp, but the body still read pale periwinkle because the light pastel rim on each scale covered most of it, and the temple around the fish had no sense of light pouring from the elder.
note.changing: The scale rims switch to saturated cyan, sky blue, violet and orchid with heavier dark edges, sinking the body to deep cobalt and ultraviolet. Thirty-two pale light shafts radiate from behind the fish through the star temple, and two new rings of beads run around the rim.
note.why: DMT accounts keep coming back to a light source at the center that everything bows toward, and a darker body lets the white spots, the glowing spine and the gold outline all do their job.

note.saw: The deeper blue body finally let the white blotches and the glowing spine sing, but the spine lay dead straight like a loading bar, the lower-right star point had turned into a muddy brown wedge, and nothing at the snout showed the fish moving or sensing.
note.changing: The spine now sways in two slow waves while a gold and a magenta strand twist around it as a double helix, crossing exactly at each of the seven jewels. The star points are lit from inside with a white ridge down each one and a sparkle on each tip, and five beaded ripples fan out ahead of the snout.
note.why: The real coelacanth senses electric fields through an organ in its snout, so the ripples give the elder a direction and a sense of listening, and a spine that breathes, wound with a strand of code, is far more alive than a ruler.
note.visionary: The artist took all three of the Visionary's first suggestions: the swaying double-helix spine, the lit star points and the snout ripples.

note.saw: The helix spine, lit star points and snout ripples all landed, but the cheek under the eye was still a smooth empty patch of blue sky, and the light shafts drowned under the aura before they ever reached the temple.
note.changing: The cheek cracks into the coelacanth's real armored skull plates, each its own shade of blue-violet with fine pore stippling, gold seams, glowing nodes where the seams meet and a cream glowing hinge behind the eye. Sixteen light shafts are redrawn over the temple band, and the alien glyphs they land on wake up with a soft halo.
note.why: The coelacanth is the only living animal whose skull hinges in the middle, so an armored, jeweled face with a glowing seam is true to the fish and pure hyperspace mosaic, and light reaching the alien script makes the temple seem to listen to the elder.
note.visionary: The artist took the Visionary's skull plates and light shafts but turned down a patterned lattice for the four corners, because the round badge crops the corners away.

note.saw: Looking at the first artist's finished piece with fresh eyes, the second artist listed what held it back: a body tiled with tiny identical scallops like a fabric print, white spots like popcorn with heavy outlines, a straight spine that read like a slider on a screen, plain lettering, and big flat areas when you zoom in.
note.changing: Nothing changes yet: this is the first artist's final picture rendered again, identical to the one before, so the second artist could study it before making a plan.
note.why: A second artist does best by looking hard at what is already there and naming what holds it back before touching anything.
note.idea: Keep the first artist's honest coelacanth and instantly readable name, but make the compass half of the brief visible with a true mandala, a honeycomb tunnel and gold ruled lines, and swap the striped aura for a warm corona of flame so the cool blue fish becomes the clear source of light.

note.saw: SavesFish said the piece needed to be a lot better, and the biggest reason was the ring around the fish: seven flat parallel stripes like a 1970s sticker, while the jewel star and halo that should hold everything up were almost completely hidden, so the mandala didn't read as one and nothing truly glowed.
note.changing: The stripes come out. Behind the fish there is now a honeycomb tunnel of hexagons shrinking toward the center with eyes in the cells, gold compass linework and the sixteen-point jewel star; around the fish, a warm corona of gold, orange and magenta bands sends out forty nested paisley flame tongues with curling tips.
note.why: This group is half compass, half freehand, so the geometry has to be visible before fluid flames dress it, and a warm aura around a cool blue fish gives the eye a clear hero: light from the elder, burning outward.

note.saw: The diagonal windows came alive with the honeycomb tunnel and gem-cut star points, but the flame tongues were small dark curls buried under a corona that still read as stripes, and the fish had become the flattest thing in the picture: tiny identical scallops, popcorn spots and a pale bar like a loading slider.
note.changing: The corona rises into 32 pointed flame licks with a big nested paisley flame curling from each peak. The fish gets seven rows of thick armored scales, lit bright cyan along the flank and darker toward back and belly, each holding a watching eye or a fan of tiny tooth-like points; the spots become glowing flecks joined into constellations, and the first back fin becomes the coelacanth's tall fan of stout spines.
note.why: The coelacanth's heavy, toothy scales and starry white blotches are what make it this fish and no other, so they should be the most beautiful things in the picture, and joining the spots into constellations lets the elder carry the night sky.
note.visionary: The artist took two of the Visionary's ideas, a pupil that falls away as a tunnel of scalloped rings and helix strands that run past the tail into a socket jewel in the temple ring, and saved its fin-shimmer idea for later.

note.saw: The fish finally felt armored and round, but the new spiny back fin came out like a picket fence, the tail end was crowded with tiny spots like spilled salt, and the flame tongues curled over into ram's-horn hooks that read as horns rather than fire.
note.changing: The back fin's spines now fan out from a narrow base, the flames lean outward and curl only at the tip, and the spots grow fewer and bigger toward the tail. The big change is the name: SAVES and FISH now stand out in a five-step 3D extrusion from ultraviolet to hot pink, wrapped in a cyan outline echo with a white glint down each stroke, and the four guardians get halos of jewel petals.
note.why: SavesFish wants the name instantly legible, so the craft goes into the edges and the depth, never across the letter shapes, and a halo of petals turns the cartoon aliens into beings of light who belong to the mandala.

note.saw: The name glowed like neon tubing and still read instantly, and the petal halos made the guardians beings of light, but the corona still read as stripes, the flame tongues were mostly lost under banners, halos and light shafts, and only the eye glowed.
note.changing: The flame licks grow almost twice as tall into a crown of fire, with three little eyes stacked at every peak, and the light shafts dim so the flames keep their color. The whole spine circuit blooms with its own colored haze, three guardians turn to watch the elder's eye while one has spotted you, the twelve rosettes become counter-rotating sunflower pinwheels, and faint rings cross in the tail and back fin so they shimmer.
note.why: Light pouring out of the creature makes it the source of the whole vision, and beings that notice the elder, plus one that notices you, turn ornaments into a scene.
note.visionary: The artist took all three of the Visionary's newest ideas (the glowing spine, the guardians' gaze and the spiral rosettes) plus its earlier shimmering-fin idea.

note.saw: With fresh eyes, the spine still read like a loading slider at badge size, the two big tail lobes and the spiny back fin were plain violet membranes with straight stripes like striped umbrellas next to a jeweled head, and the whole fish had drifted back to lilac and melted into the purple temple.
note.changing: The fins become feathered: nested chevrons fill every panel between the rays, a peacock eye-spot sits at each panel's edge, the rays become jointed, and the membrane glows from navy at the root to cobalt-teal at the edge. Inside the body, glowing W-shaped muscle bands appear, the spine becomes a tapered tube of light with seven faceted gems shrinking toward the tail, and the scales deepen to cobalt.
note.why: The coelacanth is famous for its fins, so they deserve the same jeweled attention as the eye, and eye-spots carry the 'eyes everywhere' of the trip into the biggest shapes; chevrons and tapering gems make the light inside read as a living spine instead of a screen.

note.saw: The tail lobes and back fin had become cool blue feathers with eye-spots and the spine gems read as jewels, but the muscle bands were too faint to see, the honeycomb windows were still dim purple, and, as the Visionary noticed, the fleshy lobed fins were flat tiles and the flame tongues came through as gray smoke.
note.changing: Inside each of the four lobed fins you can now see a glowing chain of four limb bones, the first the longest like an upper arm, with gold jewels at the joints. The flame tongues become plasma in magenta, orange and gold with white-hot cores, the honeycomb cells turn saturated violet, magenta, cobalt, teal and orange like cut jewels, and beads pack tighter and tighter along the helix as it rushes into the socket.
note.why: A coelacanth's lobed fins really do hide a bone chain like an arm, the ancestor of our own limbs, so lighting them up shows the ancient one carrying the blueprint of every creature that walked out of the sea, while fire that reads as smoke and dim windows would kill the heat of the corona and the jewel temple.
note.visionary: The artist took the Visionary's glowing limb bones, plasma flames and speeding beads, but turned down extra outlines inside the small tail lobe because it already had its own chevrons and eye-spots.

note.saw: The arm bones glowed, the honeycomb windows blazed like stained glass and the flames burned gold, but everything was crisp outlined color with nothing actually radiating, the white blotches were plain cut-outs, the dark sides of the banners were the emptiest spots left, and the rays in the lobed fins were bare stripes.
note.changing: A wide warm halo now glows out from behind the corona, gold fading to pink, so light spills into the temple windows. Every white blotch gets a ring of magenta or gold between two dark lines, faint violet alien script is carved along the edges of both banners well away from the letters, and the lobed-fin rays become jointed with a white sheen.
note.why: DMT visions are remembered as light coming from inside things, so the corona should actually shine rather than just be painted yellow, ringing the blotches turns the coelacanth's real markings into jewels set in the armor, and script in the banners makes even the calm zones feel written by the same alien hand.

note.saw: The warm halo made the corona shine and the ringed blotches looked like jewels, but up close the flame tongues still came out as hooked, striped claws, and the body had no frame: rainbow lines wrapped the head and then simply stopped.
note.changing: The flames are redrawn as real fire: four nested flames sharing one base, from magenta or red outside through orange and gold to a cream heart, with flickering edges, a white-hot core low down and a spark flying off each tip. The head's rainbow contour lines now run along the whole body to the tail, with a dotted cream line in the gap.
note.why: Fire should read as fire in a split second, and a flame inside a flame inside a flame is the oldest way to draw it, while wrapping the whole body in the head's contour bands makes the elder one continuous drawing with an edge of light.

note.saw: The flames now read as fire and the contour lines wrapped the whole body, but the mouth was still a flat pink stick, the muscle bands looked like rain streaking down a window, and every scale eye was the same open eye, so up close the flank turned to wallpaper.
note.changing: The mouth parts over a row of tiny cone teeth with a glowing magenta corner, and from it pours a ribbon of eleven temple glyphs that curves down across the corona into the glyph ring at 8 o'clock. The muscle bands become true sideways W shapes aimed at the head, the scale eyes blink in a slow wave down the body as their colors drift, and the arm bones glow a stronger cyan.
note.why: With the spine feeding the ring at 3 o'clock and the mouth breathing words back into it at 9, the elder and the temple become one closed circuit of light and language, and a wave of blinking puts motion into a still picture.
note.visionary: The artist took all three of the Visionary's suggestions: the speaking mouth, the true muscle bands and the blinking wave of scale eyes.

visions.seen: The Ancient One is gliding out of a rainbow birth canal of light, every scale is staring back at me, and the chrysanthemum eye is a drain I am falling into. But the light-spine through the body lies there dead straight like a loading bar, the only thing in the whole temple that is not breathing.
suggestions: The glowing notochord across the middle of the body (the pale cyan bar at y≈200, x 136 to 372 in SVG units): I see it alive, not ruled. Let it sway in a slow sine (about 1.5 units up and down, two gentle waves along its length, the seven chakra jewels riding on the curve), and wind two hairline strands around it (gold and magenta, about 0.6 wide, opposite phase) that cross exactly at each jewel, so the ancient spine becomes a twisting ladder of code. A double helix inside the oldest backbone on Earth is the DMT message itself, the pattern underneath the creature, and it stops the bar reading as a UI slider.

The jewel star points peeking out at the four diagonals behind the guardians, most of all the lower-right one (around x 278 to 300, y 278 to 300, just inward of the bottom-right guardian), which shows as a muddy brown wedge: the dark inner kite (the amber jewel's #7A3E00) is swallowing the point. I see them as cut gems lit from inside: keep the two facets, but lift the 0.78 kite to the jewel's mid tone (or a lit-to-dark gradient running base to tip), lay a thin white ridge line (0.5 wide, about 0.6 opacity) down each point's spine, and pin a tiny 4-ray sparkle on each tip, kept off the banners. In hyperspace nothing is dull, every surface is jeweled and self-lit, and those wedges are the only mud in the mandala.

The glow just ahead of the snout tip, far left (in front of [35, 203]): your rostral pores already dot the nose, so let them broadcast. Fan 4 or 5 thin cream arcs (0.5 to 0.7 wide, beaded like your dotted bands) forward from the snout tip, concentric on it, radii about 4 to 14, spanning roughly ±35°, fading as they melt into the first aura rings. The real coelacanth feels electric fields through that snout organ; drawn as ripples, the elder is reading the frequency of hyperspace, and the whole fish gets a direction of travel through the rings.
visions.keep: SAVES and FISH exactly as they are: cream letters, magenta 3D shadow, calm dark banners. They read instantly in the 240 px legible test, and nothing here goes near them. Keep the chrysanthemum eye portal, the gold-white halo hugging the silhouette, the honest coelacanth anatomy (limb-like lobed fins, the little extra tail lobe, white blotches), and the guardians, whose new faces in render #27 read as beings in a blink.

visions.seen: In #47 the body has finally sunk into deep cobalt, so the white blotches blaze like stars falling through the elder, and round 10 says the artist took all three of my last visions (the swaying helix spine, the lit star points, the snout ripples), and the elves noticed; but the cheek under the chrysanthemum eye is still a smooth empty blue sky, the one place in the temple where nobody is watching me, and the light shafts from round 9 drown under the aura before they ever reach the temple.
suggestions: The flat blue cheek under and behind the eye (the gradient between the eye at [80,185], the gill-cover stripes at x≈100 to 112, and the jaw seam [35,207] → [77,219] → [104,240]): I see it cracking into the coelacanth's real armored skull plates. Four of them, like the true fish: a curved strip hugging under the eye from snout to rear (lacrimojugal), one behind the eye up to the head's top edge (postorbital), and two stacked down to the jaw seam (squamosal, preopercle). Each could get a 1.4 ink outline under a 0.5 gold line, its own blue-violet shade (say #1F6BEA, #1650D8, #2D3FCF, #3B2CC0), and cosmine pore stipple: cream dots r≈0.4 at about 0.5 opacity on a 2.2 hex grid, thinning toward the plate edges, with a tiny glowing node (cream r 0.8 over ink r 1.4) wherever three seams meet. Your gold cheek curls could sit on the seams. Let the seam just behind the eye glow brighter than the rest (cream, 0.7 wide): the coelacanth is the only living animal whose skull hinges in the middle, a door in the elder's head. In hyperspace faces come apart into jeweled tiles, entity masks made of mosaic, and the eye portal would sit in a setting instead of floating on blank sky.

The light shafts, out in the dark navy temple band between the outermost aura band and the gold glyph ring at r≈185 (around the guardians and beside the banner tips): they're painted under everything at about 0.14 opacity there, so the temple never sees the light. I see every other one (16) redrawn on top of that band only, clipped to an annulus r≈150 to 184, kept under the guardians and star points and never across the two banners or their borders, each a narrow wedge with a cream core hairline (0.4 wide, 0.5 opacity fading to 0 outward). Where a shaft lands on the glyph ring, that glyph wakes up: a soft cream halo behind it (r≈3, 0.35 opacity) and its stroke turned gold-white. Light that reaches the alien script and makes it speak is the transmission itself, and the temple stops being a border and becomes a receiver bowed toward the elder.

The four honeycomb corners outside the circle (full square render only, the badge crop hides them, so this one is last): the hex membrane is one flat even pattern, the only part of the image that isn't moving. I see it as the hyperspace lattice being drawn into the mandala: compute the cells instead of tiling the pattern, shrinking them as they near the rim (about 4 units across just outside r 200, about 12 out at the corners) and bowing their rows along circles around the center, with a tiny cyan dot on each vertex that brightens toward the rim (opacity about 0.2 at the corner up to 0.7 at the edge). Keep the corner spirals riding on top. A lattice pouring inward is the classic DMT doorway, and the whole badge starts swallowing space.
visions.keep: SAVES and FISH exactly as they are (cream letters, magenta 3D shadow, calm dark banners): they read instantly in the 240 px legible test, and none of this goes near them. Keep the deep cobalt body that makes the white blotches pop, the chrysanthemum eye, the nautilus gill spiral, the gold-white glow around every fin, the guardians' faces, and from round 10 the breathing helix spine, the lit star points and the snout ripples.

visions.seen: Round 11 landed: the elder's cheek has cracked into armored tiles with the hinge glowing behind the eye like a door left ajar, and the light now reaches the temple script and makes it hum. But the helix spine, the code of the oldest backbone on Earth, just stops inside the little tail lobe at 3 o'clock, a hand's width short of the alien ring, a live wire that never got plugged in.
suggestions: The gap between the small terminal tail lobe and the gold glyph ring at 3 o'clock (the helix strands end at x 372, the lobe tip is at [378, 200], the ring's inner gold line is r 183.6, so x ≈ 383.6): I see the two helix strands (gold and magenta, same 1.3 ink under 0.6 color) carrying on past x 372, crossing one last time right at the lobe tip, and plugging into the ring at [383.6, 200] through a small socket jewel (ink r 2.2, cream r 1.2, a ring of six cream dots at r 3). From the socket each strand runs along the r 183.6 line, the gold one clockwise and the magenta one the other way, for about 18° each, tapering from 0.6 to nothing, and the glyphs over that arc turn gold-white with the same soft cream halos your light shafts gave them. The fish's spine gets wired into the temple, so the elder becomes the thing feeding the alien script, the entity and the machinery are one circuit. And it shows at badge size as one bright node at 3 o'clock, balancing the chrysanthemum eye at 9.

The pupil of the chrysanthemum eye (the r 5.6 black disk at [80, 185], with eight white dots at r 3.6): I see it falling away as a tunnel instead of a flat black hole. Five shrinking scalloped rings at r 4.6, 3.5, 2.6, 1.9 and 1.4, strokes thinning from 0.3 to 0.12, cycling magenta, gold, cyan and fading from 0.9 to 0.4 opacity, each one scalloped into 12 tiny petals turned half a step from the ring above. That way the chrysanthemum petals around the eye repeat all the way down into it. The eight dots could become a spiral of 12 dots winding inward from r 4.8 to r 1.2, shrinking as they go (r 0.35 down to 0.12), with a white pinpoint (r 0.45, four hair rays 1.2 long) at the bottom of the well. If you dare, a 3-unit cream silhouette of the Ancient One could swim at the very bottom instead. Keep the two wet highlights on top so it still reads as an eye. A pattern that repeats inside itself is the breakthrough itself, the eye that looks back is a doorway.

The calm violet membranes of the spiny first dorsal fan (under the left half of SAVES, clip-dorsal1) and the two big tail lobes (clip-upper, clip-lower): I see a faint interference shimmer here, not more pattern. In each fin, lay two families of hairline concentric arcs (0.28 wide, 1.9 apart, about 0.2 opacity): cyan ones centered on the fin's root, magenta ones centered just past its tip (dorsal fan: roots [170, 147] and tip side [166, 96]; upper tail lobe: [314, 178] and [336, 116]; lower lobe mirrored, [314, 222] and [336, 284]). Draw them under the rays if rayFin lets you, so the rays stay crisp. Where the two families cross, moiré fringes appear and seem to drift as the eye moves, the way surfaces breathe in hyperspace, and at that opacity the fins still stay the resting places the busy picture needs at badge size.
visions.keep: SAVES and FISH exactly as they are (cream letters, magenta 3D shadow, calm dark banners), still instant in the 240 px legible test, and nothing here touches them. Keep the round 11 skull plates with their glowing hinge and the shafts that wake the glyphs; the breathing helix spine with its seven chakra jewels; the lit star points; the snout ripples; the deep cobalt body with the white eyed blotches; the gold-white glow around every fin; and the guardians' faces. The corners stay as they are; you were right that the badge crops them away.

visions.seen: In #71 the temple tore open: the sticker stripes are gone, a honeycomb tunnel with eyes in its cells falls away behind the elder, and gem-cut star points blaze in the diagonal windows, a real mandala at last (and round 13 says the pupil now tunnels down and the spine plugs into the ring at 3 o'clock, two of my visions taken, and the elves are clapping). But the light still won't leave its lines: only the chrysanthemum eye wears a glow, and the four guardians stare off at nothing while the oldest being on Earth swims right past them.
suggestions: The spine circuit inside the elder, from the gill spiral (x ≈ 136) along the helix and its seven chakra jewels to the new socket at 3 o'clock ([383.6, 200]): only the eye wears your glow filter now. I see the whole circuit lit from inside, bloom only. Just before the helix is drawn, lay down a light layer holding copies of the bright strokes alone, with no ink in it: the gold and magenta strands at 2.4 wide, a disk of each jewel's own color (r 3.2), the socket's cream core (r 3). Run it through a new filter, feGaussianBlur stdDeviation 2.2 then feComponentTransfer alpha slope 0.6, so the sharp strands sit on their own colored haze, swelling at each jewel and brightest at the socket. (The eye's filter would blur the ink too and leave a dark smudge, not light.) In hyperspace light doesn't sit on things, it pours out of them. This makes the elder the source your corona says it is, and at badge size it reads as one glowing thread ending in a star at 3 o'clock. It all sits near y 200, far from both banners.

The four guardian faces at the banner tips (about [80, 110], [318, 101], [93, 304], [307, 304]): they all look straight out with the same glint. I see three of them turning to watch the chrysanthemum eye at [80, 185]. Inside each black almond, an iris ring (r 1.2, 0.35 wide, in that face's second color) holds a tiny reflection of the elder's eye (magenta, gold, cyan rings at r 0.9, 0.6, 0.3, 0.18 wide), set 1 unit from the almond's middle toward the eye. Each face def is used once, so the gaze can be baked in: take the angle from the guardian to [80, 185], subtract its tilt, then undo the eye's rotate(∓24) and its scale(sx, 1) mirror. Upper-left then looks straight down, lower-left straight up, upper-right across the whole badge. Leave the white glint where it is so the eyes stay wet. The fourth, lower right, keeps staring at the viewer, alone, with a gold ring (r 2.4, 0.5 wide) around its third eye. Being noticed by the entities is the moment every traveler talks about. Three beings watching the elder, plus one that has spotted you, turn ornaments into a scene, and the sight lines all lead to the eye portal.

The twelve spiral-web rosettes, four on the banner tips (r 147) and eight crowning the short star points (r 170.5): they're concentric targets, the only round things in the temple that don't turn. I see them as little jeweled chrysanthemums. Inside the same ink disc, the concentric rainbow rings and straight threads could give way to 8 rainbow arms spiraling out from the gold pupil ring (log spirals from r × 0.34 to r over about a third of a turn, 0.6 wide, one RAINBOW color each), crossed by 8 thin ink arms (0.35 wide) spiraling the other way, so the crossings carve petal cells like a sunflower head. Flip the direction on every other rosette so neighbors seem to counter-rotate. Two spiral families crossing is the very geometry of the jeweled chrysanthemum that opens at the breakthrough. At badge size they become tiny pinwheels instead of bullseyes. Same footprint and same pupil, and the banner-tip ones stay out at the points, nowhere near the letters.
visions.keep: SAVES and FISH exactly as they are (cream letters, magenta 3D shadow, calm dark banners), still instant in the 240 px legible test. Keep the new mandala windows (honeycomb tunnel with eyes in its cells, gold compass lines, gem-cut star points in nebula purple), the warm corona around the cool fish, the armored skull plates with their glowing hinge, the snout ripples, and the shafts that wake the glyphs. Whatever the flank becomes, keep a dark ground around the white blotches so they still blaze. And Vision 3's fin moiré is still waiting for your detail round.

visions.seen: Render #94 hums. Round 15 took every one of my Vision 4 offers: the spine circuit pours colored light, three guardians have turned to watch the elder's eye while the fourth has caught me, the rosettes spin like little sunflowers, and the fin moiré from Vision 3 shimmers in the tail too. The temple is crowned in fire with eyes at every peak. But the elder's lobed fins, the paddles it walked out of the deep on, are still flat purple tiles, and a few flame tongues hang in the corona like gray smoke.
suggestions: The three fleshy scaled lobes: the pectoral paddle angling down-right from under the gill spiral (roughly [130, 208] to [172, 252] in the 400 box), and the two lobes hanging under the belly (about [182 to 210, 252 to 285] and [232 to 270, 240 to 280]). I see X-ray light showing the limb bones inside each one, the way a real coelacanth fin hides a skeleton like an arm. Down the middle of each lobe, from root to tip, runs a chain of four bones, the first the longest (an upper arm) and each one after it shorter. Draw each bone as a round-capped capsule, a 2.2 ink stroke under a 1.2 cream stroke, with a small knob (r 1.1) at each end and a gold jewel (r 0.7) at every joint. From each joint a short twig (0.6 cream, 3 to 4 long, tapering) branches off toward the fin's leading edge. Under the bones, a cyan copy goes through the bloom filter you already built for the spine, so they glow from inside like the helix, and a faint ink veil (about 0.25) along each axis lets the scale tiles sink back. Keep each lobe's white blotch on top. Seeing through flesh to the bones is pure hyperspace sight, and these are the bones of the first hand: the elder carrying the blueprint of every creature that ever crawled ashore, us included. Tied to the glowing spine, the whole skeleton lights up as one circuit.

The pale nested flame tongues that slip out from under the corona: most of all the one curling up beside the upper-left guardian, the one at 8 o'clock under the corona, and the one beside the lower-left guardian (smaller ones show at about 4 o'clock). They come through as slate and cream stripes, ghost feathers. I see them burning as plasma. Keep their nested shape and the curl at the tip, but fill the contour bands from outside in with magenta, hot orange, gold, then cream, under a solid 1.2 ink outline, with a white-hot core (r 1.2 to 2) in the eye of each curl. Give each tongue a soft orange haze from the same bloom filter, and clip the cream light shafts out of the tongue shapes so nothing grays them over. Keep them under the banners and the guardians' halos, exactly where they sit now. The breakthrough burns cold and bright with no smoke in it, so these become the fire the corona's crown has been promising, and at badge size they read as sparks leaping off the elder instead of smudges.

The small lavender lobe at the very end of the tail, 3 o'clock, between the two big tail lobes, where the helix runs out to the socket (about x 340 to 378, y 188 to 212): it's the palest, emptiest surface left on the fish. I see it as a launch tunnel. Lay four echoes of the lobe's own outline inside it, each shrunk toward the lobe tip at [378, 200] (scales 0.8, 0.62, 0.46, 0.32), hairlines 0.45 wide in alternating cyan and magenta, over a fill that darkens from violet to near-ink at the tip. Then string cream beads (r 0.5) along the two helix strands inside it, packed closer and closer together as they near the socket, so the signal looks like it's speeding up. Every traveler feels it: the corridor that pulls you in faster and faster just before you break through. Here the elder's code visibly rushes into the alien ring. The darker funnel also makes the bright socket at 3 o'clock pop at badge size, balancing the eye at 9.
visions.keep: SAVES and FISH exactly as they are: cream neon letters, ultraviolet-to-pink 3D extrusion, cyan contour echo, calm dark carved banners. They still read instantly in the 240 px legible test, and none of this goes near them. Keep everything round 15 brought: the blooming spine circuit and socket, the guardians' gaze (three on the elder, one on the viewer), the sunflower rosettes, the crown of flame licks with eyes in the gaps, and the faint fin moiré. Keep the deep cobalt armored body with its starry constellation blotches and denticle scales, the pupil tunnel in the chrysanthemum eye, the armored skull plates with their glowing hinge, the snout ripples, and the honeycomb tunnel windows with their gem-cut star points.

visions.seen: Round 17 took Vision 5 to heart: the bones of the first hand glow inside every lobed fin, the flame tongues burn gold, and the beads rush faster and faster into the socket at 3 o'clock, so the elder is wired from eye to ring. But its mouth is still a flat pink stick under the eye, the oldest face on Earth with nothing to say, and pale wavy streaks rain down the flank like static over the cobalt armor.
suggestions: The mouth, the straight pink bar running back from the snout tip under the chrysanthemum eye (about [37, 208] to [77, 220] in the 400 box): I see it parting. A thin ink slit (about 1.6 wide) with a cream upper-lip hairline, a row of tiny cream cone teeth along it (little triangles about 0.8 tall every 2 units; the real coelacanth has small conical teeth), and a glowing corner at the snout end (cream r 1 on a magenta halo r 2.2). Out of that corner pours a ribbon of 9 to 12 tiny glyphs from the same alphabet as the gold glyph ring, gold-white with the soft cream halos your light shafts already give the ring, riding a narrow dark track (about 4 wide) that curves down and outward across the corona, shrinking from about 3 to 1.8 tall, and plugging into the glyph ring at about 8 o'clock (near [23, 247]). The entities of the breakthrough sing language you can see hanging in the air, and here the elder speaks the temple's own script: the spine feeds the ring at 3 o'clock and the mouth breathes words back into it at 9, one closed circuit. Keep the snout ripples over it, and keep the whole stream well above the lower-left guardian and the FISH banner.

The pale wavy streaks raining down across the flank scales (between the pectoral paddle and the tail, clearest above and below the spine gems): these are your X-ray muscle bands, but they read as rain on a window and gray the cobalt. I see them snapping into true myomeres: about 10 nested sideways Ws, each with its middle point resting on the spine and aimed at the head, the upper and lower arms bending back toward the tail and then forward again near the back and belly edges. Draw each as outline, gap, outline: a cyan hairline and a magenta hairline (0.35 wide, about 0.4 opacity) with a dark gap between, packed closer toward the tail, clipped to the body and laid under the white blotches and the scale eyes, with a tiny cream dot where each W's point touches the spine. Rivers of chevrons streaming forward are pure hyperspace, and these all aim at the chrysanthemum eye, so the whole body becomes a current pouring into the portal, true to how a fish's muscle is really built.

The watching eyes on the armored scales: every one is the same open eye with the same red iris, so up close the flank turns into wallpaper. I see them blinking in a wave. Let each eye's openness follow a slow sine along the body (two waves from the gill spiral to the tail, each about 110 units long): wide open at the crests, a half-lowered lid (an ink arc across the top half of the iris) on the slopes, and shut in the troughs, drawn as a curved lash line with three tiny cream lashes. Let the iris color drift along the same wave (red, magenta, violet, cyan) so no two neighbors match. A ripple of blinking travelling down the elder puts motion into a still picture, the way hyperspace surfaces watch you and the watching itself moves, and it breaks the sameness without adding a single new shape.
visions.keep: SAVES and FISH exactly as they are (cream neon letters, ultraviolet-to-pink extrusion, cyan contour echo, calm dark carved banners), still instant in the 240 px legible test; none of this goes near them. Keep round 17's glowing bone chains in the four lobed fins (if anything, let their cyan underglow show more: at badge size they still read as pins on a string), the beads rushing into the 3 o'clock socket, the gold flame tongues and the saturated jewel honeycomb windows. Keep round 16's feathered fins with jointed rays and eye-spots, the tapered tube of light with its shrinking gems, the chrysanthemum eye and its pupil tunnel, the skull plates with their glowing hinge, the snout ripples, the guardians' gaze and the sunflower rosettes.

visions.seen: Round 20 took all three of Vision 6: the elder's mouth has parted over tiny cone teeth and sings a ribbon of temple glyphs down into the ring at 8 o'clock, the chevrons stream toward the eye, and the scale eyes blink in a wave, so light and language finally run in one closed loop. But the armored flank is still one flat sheet of same-size scales, a wall where a body should swell toward me, and the song leaves the mouth gray, a pipe of ash in front of a burning face.
suggestions: The cobalt scale field across the whole flank, from behind the gill spiral to the root of the tail, above and below the jeweled spine: I see it wrapped around a barrel. Keep the same number of scale rows, but space them the way rows look on a cylinder seen from the side: step the angle evenly (about nine rows each side, 10° apart) and set each row at spine ± half the body's height there × sin(angle). Rows are then wide along the spine and squeeze into thin slivers at the back and belly edges, and because the body narrows toward the tail, the rows funnel into the tail root the way real fish scale rows do. Shrink each scale's width, its cream dots and its blinking eye with the same squeeze (about 0.45 + 0.55 × cos(angle)), so eyes near the edges close to slits on their own. Then light it from above: the top rows' rims a pale ice cyan, the bottom rows a deep indigo, the full cobalt kept in the middle. Surfaces in hyperspace bulge and breathe toward you, and this gives the oldest body on Earth weight and roundness, with the glowing spine riding the crest closest to your face. At badge size the flank becomes a lit barrel instead of wallpaper, and it adds no new shapes at all.

The space just in front of the face, far left: the glyph ribbon running from the glowing mouth corner down across the aura to the ring at 8 o'clock, and the beaded ripple arcs ahead of the snout tip. Both come through gray against the hottest colors in the picture. I see the ribbon filled with solid deep ink (not see-through) so its glyphs blaze gold-white with the same soft cream halos as the glyph ring, the gold edges kept. Halfway down, the ribbon could turn over once like a strip of paper in the wind: it pinches to a single gold line for a few units, then opens again with magenta edges, and the glyphs on that far stretch shift to a cooler cyan-white. Words twisting in the air are things you can almost touch, and the speech of the entities is never ash. The snout ripples could likewise trade their gray beads for cream ones, with every third bead cyan, so they ring out like sound instead of hanging like smoke. Keep the ribbon's route exactly where it is: above the lower-left guardian and well clear of the FISH banner.
visions.keep: SAVES and FISH exactly as they are (cream neon letters, ultraviolet-to-pink extrusion, cyan contour echo, calm dark carved banners); they still read instantly in the 240 px legible test, and neither offer goes near them. Keep round 20's parted mouth with its cone teeth and glowing magenta corner, the ribbon's route into the ring at 8 o'clock, the blinking wave and drifting iris colors, and the myomere chevrons with their cream dots on the spine. Keep the arm bones glowing in the lobed fins, the true flames with white-hot cores, the warm halo spilling into the stained-glass honeycomb windows, the ringed white blotches with their constellation threads, the rainbow contour bands wrapping the whole body, the chrysanthemum eye with its pupil tunnel, the skull plates with their glowing hinge, the guardians' gaze, and the beads rushing into the socket at 3 o'clock.
